Welcome to the Skills Hub
At The Skills Hub, we are proud to be a nurturing and inclusive learning community, dedicated to supporting young people whose journey in education has not always been straightforward. As an alternative provision, we recognise that every learner arrives with their own experiences, strengths, and aspirations, and it is our role to help them rediscover confidence, purpose, and success.
Our vision is rooted in Excellence through Compassion. We believe that with the right support, guidance, and opportunities, every young person can thrive. Through a personalised and engaging curriculum, we empower our students to develop not only academic skills, but also the resilience, independence, and emotional understanding needed for life beyond school.
At the heart of everything we do is a strong commitment to creating a safe and supportive environment. We place the highest importance on the wellbeing of our students, ensuring they feel valued, respected, and protected at all times. Our safeguarding culture is embedded in daily practice, creating the conditions for consistent, meaningful progress.
We are incredibly proud of our students and the achievements they make, often against significant challenges. Their achievements, both big and small, are a testament to their determination and the dedication of our staff.
We encourage you to explore our website further, where you will find useful information and guidance on a range of areas, including safeguarding and wellbeing, bursaries, online safety, and support from external agencies and stakeholders.
Thank you for taking the time to learn more about The Skills Hub. We look forward to working in partnership with families, schools, and the wider community to help every young person realise their full potential.
We aim for our young people to lead a happy and holistically prosperous life by developing the skills for them to move successfully along their life journeys. This includes academic outcomes that reflect the best of their abilities, being able to sustain relationships and employment and maintain healthy households.

Testimonials
A note of thanks for all your time and energy with our family. You guys were a welcome change in direction! I appreciated so much to be heard without judgement and your efforts to meet me where I was so I could move forwards for my son. I see your space as somewhere which should be accessed sooner rather than later; not an end of the road solution. Your work I see SHOULD be available much sooner for young people struggling not just when they’re excluded.
The Skills Hub has been the best thing that has happened to my son; the support and kindness you have all shown him and I, is second to none, no judgment, no prejudice, just pure empathy, understanding and upmost support and for that I am eternally grateful.
As a parent of a child who struggled in primary and secondary main stream schools academically and socially, I think this school is amazing, instead of labelling and rejecting it's students for their behaviours, it focuses and encourages their real talents to come to life. This school sees every student as an individual and works towards getting the best out of them with patience, time and understanding. My child has thrived and reached so many academic and personal goals that she is finally who she wants to be and is happier, so thank you.
I would like to tell you that after just 3 weeks at The Skills Hub my son has changed his whole look on life. He suffers a lot with his mental health and anxiety. He has not been happy in education since leaving primary school 2 years ago. His experience at senior school has been a roller coaster of emotions. His anxiety was effecting his attendance as well as his behaviour. I used to have to deal with major melt downs and very severe behaviours. His whole life has turned full circle and I have got my boy back. This is all thanks to your school and fantastic staff.

Careers Guidance
Careers Guidance at The Skills Hub
Careers Guidance at The Skills Hub
At the Skills Hub we are committed to providing a range of opportunities to enhance academic attainment and help prepare our students with the skills and knowledge required for their future careers. Our aim is to guide our students in making informed choices and decisions about their next steps and to open their eyes to the world of possibilities after leaving school. We work towards preparing our students to face the ever-changing world of work by encouraging them to become global thinkers and ensure they continue learning and developing at The Skills Hub and beyond.
We have our own experienced in-house careers advisor who is trained to support our students with any study or career related choices. Our careers provision is tailored to each year group, ensuring individual students receive relevant and timely support at their stage of education. Year 10 and Year 11 students can undertake work-based experiences and opportunities and will participate in vocational courses for example Mechanics or Hair and Beauty. In addition to this they will also be enabled to explore different virtual work experience opportunities offered by different employers. Year 11 students will also receive comprehensive support and advice on apprenticeships or further education. At the Skills Hub, we pride ourselves on the continuous and highly personalised support we offer our past year 11 students’ post-graduation, which gives them access to regular one-to-one meetings with a dedicated Transitions Officer.
Our careers programme ensures that all students have equal opportunities by having regular access to a wide range of employers, further and higher education institutions and independent training providers. We work closely with local businesses as well as the West London Careers Hub who provide us with regular and up to date labour market information and support the development of employability skills for our young people by helping us to access a range of work experience placements for our students and employability workshops that are delivered at our school. We regularly organise career related activities such as CV and job interview skills workshops and welcome relevant guest speakers who share inspirational life stories and career journeys.
If you would like to find out more about Careers Guidance at The Skills Hub, please contact Rouna Ali.
E: rali@theskillshub.org
The Careers Programme is reviewed annually in the Spring Term.

Gatsby Benchmarks
Our approach to the Gatsby Benchmarks
The Gatsby Benchmarks is a framework that schools and colleges can use to develop a good careers programme. As part of the statutory careers requirements, every school should aim to meet the 8 Gatsby Benchmarks, which we at the Skills Hub strive to do. Besides our dedicated careers lead, we also receive regular continual professional development for all our staff that helps our teachers cover careers as part of their curriculum delivery.
A stable careers programme: At the Skills Hub we have an embedded programme of career education and guidance that is known and understood by students, teachers and further stakeholders.
Learning from career and labour market information: Our students and staff have access to good quality information about future study options and labour market opportunities. We ensure all our staff cover careers in the curriculum so that they can support our students in accessing relevant information.
Addressing the needs of each student: Our students receive internal- and external careers guidance throughout their time at the Skills Hub. Advice and support gets tailored to the needs of each student, ensuring we adhere to our school values of equality and diversity throughout any programme. For example, the experts we welcome every few months to work on our students’ career action plans.
Linking curriculum learning to careers: All staff at the Skills Hub receive continuous professional development sessions that help us link curriculum learning with careers. STEM subject teachers are expected to highlight the relevance of STEM subjects for a wide range of future career paths.
Encounters with employers and employees: We offer our students have multiple opportunities to learn from employers about work, employment and the skills that are valued in the workplace. We achieve this through a range of activities such as guest speakers, mentoring opportunities, and work experience placements.
Experiences of workplaces: Our students receive first-hand experiences of the workplace through work visits, work shadowing opportunities and work experience to open their eyes to the world of work.
Encounters with further and higher education: We have a yearly career fair where our students have access to a range of educators and employers. We also arrange trips to open days and ensure that our students are told about the full range of learning opportunities that are available to them, which includes both academic and vocational routes and learning in schools, colleges, universities, and in the workplace.
Personal guidance: We offer opportunities for guidance interviews with a career adviser, both in school and in professional settings. Students are supported in preparing for their chosen career area, using specific local labour market information to help them prepare for and apply for, achievable and realistic local jobs and apprenticeships.
For more information on the Gatsby benchmarks please click on the following link www.goodcareerguidance.org.uk

PSHE (inc. RE)
Personal, social, health and economic education (PSHE) is an essential part of all students’ education. At The Skills Hub, the PSHE curriculum enables all students develop the knowledge, skills and attributes they need to keep themselves healthy, safe, and prepared for life.
Our PSHE programme and the universal PHSE offer aims to have an impact on students’ academic and social outcomes. PSHE education contributes to our school’s statutory duties including the Equality Act (2010) to provide a balanced and broadly-based curriculum.
Our PSHE offer addresses; substance misuse and its dangers, healthy eating, the importance of physical and mental health citizenship, British values, budgeting and other key skills for life. These are addressed through the core themes of ‘Health and Wellbeing’, ‘Living in the Wider World’ and ‘Relationships’. Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) is embedded within our PSHE framework.
PSHE at The Skills Hub will address barriers to learning, raise aspirations, and improve the life chances of all students.
Religious Education (RE)
At The Skills Hub Religious Education (RE) is delivered in KS3 as part of Cultural Studies and the whole school in core PSHE lessons. Religion and beliefs shape our values and our behaviour. RE develops students’ knowledge and understanding of the faiths that form part of contemporary society.
It encourages young people to ask challenging questions about the meaning and purpose of life and issues of right and wrong. RE develops students’ knowledge and understanding of the principal world faiths and also contributes to students’ personal development and well-being. Students should understand and respect the range of different cultures and spirituality within the school and further afield as an essential element of their preparation for adult life in the modern world and a diverse society.
If parents/carers wish to withdraw their child from all or part of RE please contact Chiara Lane clane@theskillshub.org

Mental Health and Wellbeing
Support at The Skills Hub
The Skills Hub recognises the importance of Mental Health and Wellbeing as the basis to allow students and staff to fully reach their potential. Every two weeks we, as a staff team, nominate three students to be our Mental Health Wellbeing Ambassadors. Which in turn can be reflected in having a compassionate and individualised approach to reach the same goal but through our different curriculum pathways.
We are proud to say that we are an inclusive school, and we celebrate our differences through SMSC activities where students learn about British values, Wellbeing and Cultural Diversity. Our Mental Health Lead, Skills Coaches, Safeguarding Team and the SENCO have a particular focus on developing positive Mental Health.
The key to maintaining positive Mental Health is to show commitment we at The Skills Hub have started our journey and we are working towards a ‘Wellbeing Schools Award’.
Useful links to support positive mental health
Childline
National organisation offering online support and telephone support to young people in distress. Free phone number 0800 1111. Top Tip - you can hang up and re-dial if you don't get along with the person you are speaking to.
Children's Mental Health Week
Resources for young people, parents and carers
Mind
Free mental health support from leading UK charity. Information and support for those living with a mental health problem. Support line: 0300 102 1234 (Monday to Friday 9am to 6pm)
Royal College of Psychiatrists
Royal College of Psychiatrists website has information pages to view online and 36 fact sheets available, covering issues around growing up, parental mental illness and mental health difficulties within adolescence. This includes Mind Ed, which is a free e-learning resource to help adults to identify and understand children and young people with mental health issues.
Samaritans
The Samaritans is a national organisation which offers 24 hour telephone and face to face emotional support to people in distress. Their website offers useful information about a range of mental health issues. Call free any time, from any phone on 116 123.
Your Mental Health
Information about support for Mental Health in Hillingdon

Equality & Diversity
The Skills Hub is committed to creating an inclusive environment, where people are treated with dignity and respect and where we anticipate and respond positively to different needs and circumstances so that everyone can achieve their potential.
We are committed to promoting and advancing equality of opportunity, not only because it is an important part of the mission, vision and values of the Academy, but also because by attracting and retaining the most diverse range of students, staff and partners, we will ensure the Academy’s future success.
We believe that everyone has the right to be treated fairly and without discrimination, regardless of their circumstances or background and to be appreciated for their genuine self. In particular we make sure that all our policies and practice prevent discrimination against someone on the grounds of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, sexual orientation.
We will consult and involve the school community in our decision making.

Parents
Parents and carers are the most important people in the lives of our students. In order for our work to be successful, we depend very much on their co-operation.
Parents have a legal right and a duty to be involved in the education of their children. We encourage parents/carers to telephone or come into school to discuss any issues concerning our students.
Parents/carers are also asked to ensure that their children have a reasonable amount of sleep and arrive at the centre on time for their day. It is very helpful if we are informed in advance when a student is going to be absent for any reason. Any unexplained absences are tracked using a Truancy Call system.
Skills Coaches make regular contact with parents/carers to keep them fully informed of progress. We take every opportunity to tell parents/carers of the good work that students are doing

Attendance
Please contact the school on the first day of your Child’s absence
You can contact the school by phone or email:
E: tsh-attendance@theskillshub.org
It is vital that students attend school regularly and on time to get the best out of their education.
It is important that parents/carers appreciate that if a student does not arrive at school, teachers have no way of knowing whether that non-arrival is due to them not being sent, or due to other causes. Parents are therefore asked to contact the school on the first day that their child is absent and before school is due to start; 9.45am. Reception can be contacted on: 01895 447102.
It is also important that the school always have up to date emergency contact numbers. We ask parents/carers, if possible, to please provide more than one number and/or contact, to ensure that contact can always be made.
The school works closely with Hillingdon’s Participation Team to oversee attendance. A monthly report is produced and discussed with the Participation Team with a particular emphasis on extended or regular non-attendance.
Should a student choose to leave school, The Skills Hub has a procedure in place to ensure the safety and wellbeing of the student is paramount.

Online Safety
Keeping Safe online
Our Online Safety Policy can be found on the Policies page of this website. Alternatively, copies are available from the school office.
There is lots of information available for parents about how to keep your children safe on the internet. Explore the links below for hints, tips and discussion around e-safety issues.
Please talk to a member of staff in school if you have concerns or need help.
Online Safety Hub
The Skills Hub takes online safety very seriously. You can read our Online Safety Policy on the Policies page and find help and resources via the link below:
